text:
samir: FYI escalated from CS — customer seeing all burst credits drop to 0 within ~20s during a short ingestion burst, then sustained 429s for a few minutes. Asking for repro/debug steps and whether smoothing config could be causing over-penalization.

agnes: Customer timeline: they run a fan-out job that opens ~150 very short requests (50-200ms each) across 3 API keys over ~18s. They expect the burst cushion to absorb it but saw immediate 429s. Provided curl traces and sample rates.

samir: Posting the curl they sent (redacted key):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"prompt":"...", "max_tokens":64}'
```
They also included a short timeline: 17:02:03 to 17:02:21 many, 17:02:22 429, 17:02:50 refill ~+10 tokens but still throttled.

mei: Can you paste their request rate curve? My suspicion: many very short-lived connections cause per-request accounting to trigger smoothing bucket logic. We recently tightened the smoothing window for multi-key fanout to avoid abuse. Smoothing default is 60s with a per-key instantaneous cap + shared burst pool.

agnes: Here's the customer's approximate QPS sequence from their logs: 0.2, 1.8, 3.2, 6.5, 14.1, 9.3, 4.0, 2.6 (all within 18s). They say each request is small (avg 60 tokens).

ops-oncall: Ran the internal debug for the customer's org id (obf-123). Command: 
```
rictl quota inspect --org obf-123 --since 2026-03-01T17:00:00Z --until 2026-03-01T17:10:00Z
```
Output snapshot: 
```
time=2026-03-01T17:02:10Z key=key-aaa credits=8.4 smoothing_window=60s burst_pool=12.0
time=2026-03-01T17:02:18Z key=key-aaa credits=0.0 action=throttle code=429
```
Also saw transient per-key lock events: rl_debug: lock_acquire key-aaa ttl=2s gripe=high-concurrency.

mei: That aligns. Two things: (1) The burst pool is consumed quickly when many keys fan out because we subtract estimated token cost per request immediately (to prevent queueing exploits). For lots of tiny requests that estimate is conservative and can overspend the pool. (2) The smoothing window plus per-key instantaneous cap can cause brief refills to be ignored until the smoothing decay completes.

samir: Suggested immediate responses for customer: (a) ask them to throttle to ~8 qps across keys for 30s, (b) aggregate short requests into a single batch where possible, (c) enable request coalescing on their side (we can point to batching docs). Also offered a temporary manual uplift of burst pool while they rework pipeline. Thoughts?

agnes: Customer already able to batch some but not all. They asked for a config change rather than app code changes. Are we comfortable bumping smoothing_window or temporarily increasing their burst_pool?

mei: We can do a temporary bump to their burst_pool and lower per-key conservative estimate to reduce overcharging. Risk: exposes us briefly to higher token spend if this is abusive. Mitigation: set a time-limited flag and monitor. I can authorize a 2x burst_pool for 1 hour if support agrees.

ops-oncall: If you want to do that, I need org id + approved slack thread id. I'll also attach an alert for any >300% token delta in the next hour. Command to apply (internal):
```
rictl quota modify --org obf-123 --burst-pool 24.0 --expires-in 1h --reason "support: temporary bump for fanout repro"
```
I'll run it once we confirm.

samir: I'll propose that to the customer along with a short repro checklist they can run so we can verify: 1) run their fanout with a single key and collect per-request latencies, 2) rerun with 3 keys, 3) run rictl (we'll provide support view) to capture the rl_debug lines. If we see the same rapid deduction, we'll revert the bump and surface change to product.

agnes: Draft reply to customer: "We see the burst pool being consumed quickly because many small simultaneous requests trigger conservative cost estimates and smoothing behavior. Short-term options: throttle ~8 qps, batch requests, or accept a 1-hour temporary burst uplift while you refactor. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min call to walk through the repro and capture rl_debug traces." Would you add anything @mei? :thumbsup:

mei: Looks good. Add note that fractional refill cadence is per-second but smoothing decay is exponential over the window — so they may see credits return in small increments, not a big jump. Also link to docs: https://docs.redwood.example/inference/quotas#burst-credits-smoothing

support-bot: Ticket #45678 updated: temporary burst_pool uplift scheduled pending ops-oncall execution.

samir: Thanks team — I'll get customer approval and post here before ops runs the rictl command.
